findings.claim: The new early return in CollectGeneric (`type.OriginalDefinition.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`) is not limited to value types, so it also catches closed generic *classes* and record classes from a referenced assembly. The requirement's table lists these as rows that already worked. On base, the closed-generic branch ran `GetObjectInfo` and then `CollectCore(type.OriginalDefinition)`, so the consuming assembly generated and registered its own formatter for `Lib.Item<T>`. On head both steps are skipped, so `app`'s resolver no longer has a formatter for `Lib.Item<int>`. This breaks the criterion that the 'ok' rows keep working as before. It also matters for trimmed and NativeAOT apps when `lib` was built without the generator, or when only `app`'s resolver is in the resolver chain.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataClosedGenericClassFormatterTests.ClosedGenericClassFromReferencedAssembly_StillGetsFormatterInConsumingAssembly. It compiles `lib` with `[MessagePackObject] public class Item<T>`, references it from `app` (Cmd with an `Item<int>` member), runs MessagePackGenerator and asserts that an ItemFormatter is generated. Expected: passes on base, fails on head.

findings.claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper drops every analyzer diagnostic that has no in-source location, not only diagnostics about metadata types. Take a source `[MessagePackObject]` type in the compilation that inherits from a referenced-assembly base class whose public property has no [Key]. `GetAllMembers` yields the inherited metadata property, and `item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` is null, so the MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004, an Error per L2) location is null and the diagnostic is silently discarded. The invalid type is declared in this compilation, so L8 (which covers only types *from* referenced assemblies) does not excuse the miss. The diagnostic should fall back to the source type's identifier location instead.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a lib with `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }`. In app write `[MessagePackObject] public class Derived : Lib.Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }`. Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer and observe that no MsgPack004 is reported for the inherited X: head's ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops it because the location is Location.None (base threw AD0001 instead).
